caption:
Kitchener buyer: one missed date can end your deal.

Offer accepted? The work is not over. 1) Find the condition dates in your offer and put them in your calendar. 2) Book your home inspection right away, as inspectors can fill up. 3) Ask your lender which documents they need and by when. 4) If a condition isn't waived or extended in writing by its date, the deal can end. Ask your realtor and lawyer how your conditions work.

caption:
Sold your Etobicoke home. Where do you live until you close on the next one?

Selling and buying at once? 1) Ask whether both deals can close on the same day. 2) If they can't, plan where you'd stay and store your belongings in between. 3) Ask your lender about bridge financing, which is short-term and has costs. 4) Tell your lawyer both closing dates early so they can plan the funds.

caption:
$1M Georgetown home. What's the land transfer tax at closing?

Example: a $1,000,000 purchase, no refund. Ontario land transfer tax: $55,000 x 0.5% = $275; next $195,000 x 1% = $1,950 (running $2,225); next $150,000 x 1.5% = $2,250 (running $4,475); last $600,000 x 2% = $12,000. Total: $16,475. Provincial tax only; legal fees, title insurance and adjustments are extra, and Toronto adds its own tax.

Source: Ontario.ca, "Calculating land transfer tax" (updated Apr 22, 2026). Eligibility rules apply to refunds.

Moving up? Comment INFO to get full details, or call 905-452-4298.

Example only. Not tax or legal advice.

frames.say: Million dollar Georgetown home. Land transfer tax?
Step one. The first fifty-five thousand dollars at half a percent: two hundred seventy-five dollars.
Step two. The next one hundred ninety-five thousand at one percent: one thousand, nine hundred fifty dollars.
Step three. The next one hundred fifty thousand at one and a half percent: two thousand, two hundred fifty dollars.
Last band. The remaining six hundred thousand at two percent: twelve thousand dollars.
So all in, the land transfer tax is sixteen thousand, four hundred seventy-five dollars.

caption:
Selling before your Brampton mortgage ends? Check the penalty first.

Breaking a closed mortgage early usually means a prepayment penalty, usually the higher of three months' interest or the interest rate differential (IRD). The IRD can be much higher, so ask your lender to calculate yours before you list. Buying again? Ask whether you can port your mortgage to your new home.

Source: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, "Mortgage fees: Prepayment penalties" (page updated Oct 15, 2025).

Thinking of selling? Comment INFO to get full details, or call 905-452-4298.
